defaults.credential_transport: Credentials are accepted only in the Authorization header, the trusted proxy X-API-Key header, or the thingino_session cookie. URL query credentials are rejected.
defaults.ingress_policy: WebUI, Control, media, and snapshot routes require TLS. Management Host values are limited to IP literals, single-label local names, .local, and .home.arpa; a present Origin must match the HTTPS authority exactly. Plain HTTP remains only for ONVIF SOAP compatibility.
defaults.mutation_csrf: Every browser mutation requires application/json or X-Requested-With: Thingino-WebUI. Explicit X-API-Key and internal Authorization headers are non-browser guards, but a non-empty JSON body still requires application/json.
defaults.onvif_snapshot_auth: /onvif/image.cgi and /onvif/image1.cgi use the normal authenticated media-authorize path and do not have an internal authentication bypass.
defaults.trusted_ip_semantics: A validated nonzero CIDR or exact IP may authorize GET only. Mutations and credential management still require an explicit browser session or API key as specified by the route; paranoid disables the trusted-IP read bypass.
defaults.media_backend: Raptor is the only production media backend. It uses bounded daemon IPC and an audited host-only dispatch for runtime metadata, snapshots, day/night, checked live imaging and color, required-participant privacy, and patched IVS motion transitions with readback. Unimplemented operations return service_unavailable with a specific reason. Deprecated /api/v1/prudynt route aliases dispatch to Raptor for compatibility. WHIP uses the authenticated proxy on a port distinct from RSD 8554.
defaults.raptor_motion_skip_frame_count: The additive motion POST field skip_frame_count is an integer 0..65535 and requires enabled=true plus a current native capability. RVD changes only the Move skip-frame parameter, verifies the full SDK parameter block, and repairs its config cache. Control then requires fresh live observation, config-save and independent motion.skip_frames disk equality before persistent=true. GET adds skip_frame_count, skip_frame_count_available, saved_skip_frame_count and skip_frame_count_matches_saved. Missing native capability keeps these fields unavailable. Receipts do not establish device startup, physical cadence or detection quality.
defaults.raptor_motion_lifecycle: Control starts one in-process Raptor Motion owner before HA. It polls checked RVD status every 500 ms with a 150 ms read deadline. Each Move SDK result replaces one mutex-protected RVD snapshot containing a producer epoch, result sequence, raw positive or negative result, and timestamp. Control baselines the first result from each epoch, consumes each newly observed sequence once, ignores duplicate snapshots without producing Detected or Clear, and preserves processed state behind unavailable status on malformed replies or timeouts. Debounce counts distinct positive results observed by the poll; cooldown, initialization, minimum-active and post-event values are seconds and use the existing MotionStateMachine. Transitions use the existing broker-neutral MotionEventSink. RVD owns validated config cache and disk persistence. POST requires all five timing fields together; GET reports owner availability and saved equality. Optional destination workers consume the same processed events through independent bounded queues.
defaults.raptor_stream_audio_policy: stream0.audio_enabled and stream1.audio_enabled independently include the existing RAD microphone ring in that stream's RSD RTSP sessions and managed RMR MP4 files. An absent legacy key preserves the two prior defaults: RSD includes RTSP audio and managed RMR remains video-only. Control exposes selection_required with null shared configured, saved, active and pending values; it never adds an audio choice to an unrelated stream save. One explicit true or false choice creates the shared policy. The exact legacy owner split remains an allowed legacy_selection_pending state until restart, so explicit retry or undo stays available; any other missing or disagreeing required owner disables editing. Cold-disabled stream1 does not require an imaginary RMR1 readback. The policy does not enable or unmute RAD and does not change Privacy, WebRTC or talkback. Enabling also requires an active built RAD codec accepted by both consumers: PCM/L16, G711U/PCMU, G711A/PCMA, AAC or Opus. Control saves through RVD, reads an explicit disk key independently and confirms the active consumer policy remains unchanged without treating transient source availability as policy. A full camera-stack restart applies the saved policy because RSD SDP/session tracks and RMR mux tracks are lifecycle-bound. A late RAD ring rotates a managed video-only segment before reporting an audio track. A post-mutation failure is partial_apply and requires explicit retry.
defaults.secret_semantics: No secret is returned. Omitted, empty, or null secret fields preserve the stored value unless the route says it rotates or clears one.

routes.secret_semantics: The destination URL is write-only because it may contain a private path or query. GET returns url:null plus url_set and live_url_set. An omitted, null or empty POST URL preserves the stored value. Saving validates and starts only the dedicated bounded worker; no outbound request occurs in the HTTP request or Motion action worker.

response_schema.semantics: The Motion action worker only performs a nonblocking enqueue into a capacity-two dedicated outbound worker. One delivery uses a bounded JSON body, 500 ms connect timeout, 2 s total timeout, no redirect or proxy, and at most 4096 response bytes. HTTPS requires libcurl, the installed CA bundle, peer verification and hostname verification. Counters and result classes never reveal the URL or transport error text.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime exposes bounded counters and sanitized result classes only; the destination URL and raw library errors are never returned.

The full ntfy topic URL and optional bearer token are write-only. Empty, null or omitted secrets preserve the stored value; clear_token:true explicitly removes the token. Bearer authentication requires HTTPS. Saving never sends a notification.

response_schema.semantics: A dedicated capacity-two worker posts the fixed readable Motion detected text body to the configured ntfy topic. Delivery uses the source-profile libcurl transport with 500 ms connect and 2 s total deadlines, no proxy or redirects, HTTP(S)-only protocol limits, and at most 4096 response bytes. HTTPS verifies the peer and hostname against the installed CA bundle. No media is read or attached.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime exposes counters and sanitized result classes only. It never returns the topic URL, bearer token or raw transport error text.

The Gotify message endpoint and application token are write-only. Blank, null or omitted secrets preserve stored values; explicit clear fields remove them. Enabling requires both fields, and a token requires HTTPS with peer and hostname verification. Saving sends no notification.

response_schema.semantics: A dedicated capacity-two worker POSTs fixed Motion title and text JSON to the configured Gotify endpoint with X-Gotify-Key. Delivery has 500 ms connect and 2 s total deadlines, no proxy or redirects, a 4096-byte response cap, and verified HTTPS. A 2xx response counts as success only when its bounded JSON body has a positive Gotify message id. No media is read or attached.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime returns sanitized counters and result classes only, never the endpoint, token, request headers, response body or raw transport errors.

The bot token and chat destination are write-only. Blank, null or omitted fields preserve stored values; explicit clear fields remove them. Enabling requires both. The API target is fixed to the official verified-HTTPS Telegram Bot API. Saving sends no notification.

response_schema.semantics: A dedicated capacity-two worker POSTs fixed Motion text through Telegram Bot API sendMessage to https://api.telegram.org. Delivery has 500 ms connect and 2 s total deadlines, no proxy or redirects, a 4096-byte response cap, and verified TLS. A 2xx response counts as success only when bounded JSON reports ok true and a positive result message_id. No photo, clip or other media is sent.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime returns sanitized counters and result classes only, never the bot token, chat destination, request URL, request or response body, or raw transport errors.

Only the SMTP password is write-only. Empty, null or omitted password preserves it; clear_password:true removes it. Saving sends no email. TLS is mandatory in both explicit modes and peer and hostname verification cannot be disabled.

response_schema.semantics: A dedicated capacity-two worker sends one fixed-subject, fixed-body text message. starttls uses smtp and implicit uses smtps; CURLUSESSL_ALL, strict peer and hostname verification, the installed CA bundle, a 500 ms connect deadline and a 5 s total deadline are mandatory. Runtime libcurl must advertise both SMTP and SMTPS. CURLE_OK and a final 2xx SMTP response are both required. No custom content or media is sent.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime returns sanitized counters and result classes only, never credentials, message bytes or raw transport errors.

The FTP password is write-only. Empty, null or omitted password preserves it; clear_password:true removes it. Saving sends no file. Explicit FTPS is the only mode; plaintext fallback and certificate-verification bypass are unavailable.

response_schema.semantics: A dedicated capacity-two worker handles each active channel-1 Motion event without blocking the Motion action worker. It reads one JPEG from RHD into at most 256 KiB of memory and uploads it once with a random per-process session id plus event sequence in the fixed filename. It never spools, retries, overwrites intentionally, uploads video or accepts a filename template. Explicit FTPS requires AUTH TLS, PROT P, peer and hostname verification, the installed CA bundle, FTP-only protocol restriction, an empty proxy, no redirects, FTP_SKIP_PASV_IP=1, a 500 ms connect deadline and a 5 s total deadline. CURLE_OK plus the final 2xx STOR acknowledgement are required. Privacy off is independently read before and after capture. The final config-generation, privacy-generation and Privacy-off check holds the shared mutation lock, then releases it before DNS and upload. The same generations feed libcurl's progress callback. Cancellation is best effort: it prevents a new capture or transfer and interrupts a changed-generation transfer, but cannot recall bytes already sent.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime returns sanitized counters and result classes only. It never returns credentials, target URL, filename, JPEG bytes or raw transport errors.
Password is write-only. Success creates a Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict runtime session cookie.
The server expires only the presented runtime session cookie.
The response never contains a cookie value or password.

Password is write-only and synchronizes the root, WebUI, and ONVIF management credential for every media backend. The ONVIF file is independently read back before success; Failure restores the previous root hash and ONVIF file where possible. An unconfirmed rollback returns partial_apply and invalidates browser sessions; a confirmed rollback returns credential_update_failed. RTSP keeps its separate viewer credential. API keys cannot call this route, the browser login must be at most 10 minutes old, and success invalidates all browser sessions.

semantics.raptor: Experimental media health describes validated RVD and RHD IPC replies only; it does not assert recorder, audio, motion, RSD, RWD, RAM, image quality or physical acceptance.

routes.secret_semantics: Health metadata contains no credentials, tokens, or private configuration.

semantics.raptor_recording: Exactly one mp4.start or mp4.stop object with channel 0 or 1 selects the fixed rmr0 or rmr1 owner. Managed RMR starts idle and writes video-only continuous MP4 to a verified SD block mount under /mnt/mmcblk0p1/raptor/streamN. Start requires available storage and video. Stop remains allowed after SD loss. One mutation command is followed by bounded independent writer readback; accepted start requires real writes, accepted stop requires fully closed files. Acknowledgements or desired flags alone are not acceptance. Post-command failure returns partial_apply; no automatic command retry or persistence.
semantics.backend_busy: 503 retryable pre-apply rejection: another Control media mutation holds the lock. No command from this rejected request was issued; explicitly retry after the active change completes.
semantics.raptor_ir: Exact cmd ircut or ir850 plus integer val 0 or 1 invokes independent RIC set-output, validates its acknowledgement and a separate get-output-state. Unsupported or unavailable output rejects before mutation; post-command failures are partial_apply. No automatic retry or config-save. Filter enabled means inserted/day policy; observed completion is a pulse with released coils, not a measured motor position.
semantics.raptor_audio: A single audio.mic_enabled or audio.spk_enabled boolean invokes checked RAD ai-enable/disable or ao-enable/disable under the mutation lock. Acceptance requires independent owner readback and unchanged mute policy; post-command failures are partial_apply. No config-save or automatic retry. Missing or unknown owner is unavailable before mutation.
semantics.raptor_motion: The single motion.enabled boolean invokes patched RVD ivs-enable and requires a separate ivs-status readback with matching active and receiving. Does not persist configuration. Failed transitions and partial privacy application return partial_apply, not unsupported. Heartbeat preserves null observations with supported true; explicit privacy protection/on, explicit privacy off, and motion stop recovery targets remain available.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted.

semantics.raptor: Same three bounded queue actions and response shape. Queue acceptance does not establish broker delivery or device effect. MQTT camera commands use the same checked Privacy, Motion Guard, IR, color and day/night operations as Preview; observed readback drives retained state. Snapshot uses the guarded bounded image path.
semantics.disabled: Disabled integrations reject all three actions with HTTP 503 service_unavailable and message Home Assistant integration is disabled; actions never enable the service. Saving enabled configuration starts the connection automatically.
semantics.webui_polling: The Services HA status poll is single-flight. Actions are disabled until saved runtime confirms enabled; publishing also requires connected. Saves invalidate stale polls and refresh runtime without replacing drafts. Actions await any older poll, then request fresh state. Navigation disposes polling.

routes.secret_semantics: The request only queues bounded work for the native HA worker; it performs no broker I/O in the HTTP request worker.

semantics.backend_busy: 503 retryable pre-apply rejection: another Control media mutation holds the lock. No command from this rejected request was issued; explicitly retry after the active change completes.
semantics.raptor: status accepted requires the RIC acknowledgement and a separate matching mode/state readback. Automatic mode may report either day or night. Independently observed camera state is required to establish the physical day/night effect.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted.

No secret fields are accepted. This is Prudynt-only. Raptor warm sensor reacquisition is intentionally unsupported; after health identifies Raptor, the WebUI labels and explicitly confirms the normal reboot route instead.
No secret fields are accepted.

No secret fields are accepted. Both backends use the shared host flow: validate the overlay directory, write and fsync only .thingino-factory-reset, then schedule a normal reboot. Protected partitions and immutable identity are outside this mutation.
No secret fields are accepted. Reset metadata is shared host state for the Raptor runtime; this read does not select a media owner.

semantics.raptor: Uses the same bounded native host NTP sync as the legacy backend. Does not change the configured timezone or imply daemon timezone reload.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted.

semantics.raptor: A bounded JPEG is fetched from the loopback RHD endpoint for stream 0 or 1. Malformed upstream responses are bad_gateway; deadline exhaustion is backend_timeout.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted or returned.
The browser sends no rwd credential. Control authenticates the same-origin session, forwards only bounded SDP to loopback rwd, and rewrites the opaque session Location to the authenticated route.

request_schema.raptor: username, password, rtsp_port, rtsp_ch0, rtsp_ch1 only; validate all fields before commands; ports 80/443/8080/8555 reserved; username 1..64 printable without spaces; password 10..127 printable without surrounding spaces or space-hash; aliases 1..63 ASCII alphanumeric dot underscore hyphen with reserved names rejected; blank password omitted by UI

response_schema.raptor: GET source=raptor, password=null/password_set, auth_enabled, observed port and paths; saved_rtsp_ch0/saved_rtsp_ch1 are independently read aliases or null, with missing or empty aliases using canonical stream0/stream1 defaults; rtsp_paths_match_saved is true only when both saved paths are known and equal live paths; mic=audio, ONVIF fields null; POST status=accepted,persistent=true only after live apply/readback, config-save and all requested disk keys match

routes.secret_semantics: The RTSP viewer password is write-only. GET returns null plus password_set and never returns it. This route does not read or change the ONVIF management credential. API keys cannot access the credential-management route, and POST requires a browser login at most 10 minutes old. Raptor password disk readback is used only for internal equality and never included in HTTP replies or logs. A partial failure requires explicit retry; re-enter a changed password. Busy is a retryable pre-apply rejection.

Wi-Fi password is write-only. GET returns null plus password_set; omitted, null, or empty POST preserves it. Omitted interface and interface fields are merged with the persisted configuration before a complete file is written.

response_schema.raptor: GET adds source:raptor, timezone_reload_supported and timezone_applied booleans. Applied requires the stored name/rule and matching live rule plus January/July libc probes from every configured or socket-present daemon. POST returns status:ok,persistent:true,applied:true only after fixed-file reload, independent daemon observations and exact file readback. A missing or incompatible required daemon disables editing; a supported but mismatched timezone allows explicit retry.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted or returned. The canonical POST field is the IANA timezone name; the backend maps it through the read-only /usr/share/tz.json catalog and writes the corresponding POSIX value to /etc/TZ. When the selected IANA name changes, Control applies the mapped rule through the Raptor timezone participant reload paths. A participant socket, protocol, or deadline failure is returned as unavailable/timeout rather than reported as a successful live apply. Legacy tz_name/tz_data fields are accepted only when they exactly match a catalog entry and are not part of the canonical UI contract. Raptor uses shared file persistence followed by fixed timezone-reload commands to RVD and every configured or socket-present RSD/RHD/RAD/RIC/ROD/RMR/RMR0/RMR1/RWD; the listed participants are Raptor services. The full-stack profile declares required timezone owners independently of feature enablement; both per-channel recorders, RAD and RWD remain required while idle. ROD renders configured OSD text into bitmaps and RVD applies them; the full-stack profile starts and requires ROD. Socket-present owners remain required regardless of configuration. Participant inventory and capability preflight precede writes. Reload reads only /etc/TZ and requires exact equality with the catalog-mapped expected rule. A failure after persistence starts is partial_apply, with no automatic rollback or retry. Saving the same timezone explicitly reloads all participants again. backend_busy is a 503 pre-apply rejection. NTP synchronization, startup propagation and continuous or physical acceptance are separate.
The bounded crontab document contains commands but no credential files or generated secrets.

semantics.raptor: The Raptor runtime provides one bounded native HA service and worker. POST shares the Raptor mutation lock, persists validated partial config, then reconfigures that worker. Secret handling and unsupported entities remain unchanged.

routes.secret_semantics: mqtt.password is write-only. GET returns password:null plus password_set. Omitted, null, or empty POST password preserves the stored value. Saving only wakes the native HA worker; it performs no broker I/O in the HTTP request worker. OTA and unverified D-Link outputs are explicitly unsupported.

semantics.raptor.daynight: Requires mode:auto|day|night, with optional thresholds:{trigger:luma|gain|adc|photo,values:{all active trigger keys}} and timing:{sample_interval_ms,transition_delay_s?}. Thresholds require the existing trigger and bounded integer values. Gain requires day < night, ADC requires night < day and Photo requires day < night < deep. Trigger changes and calibration are rejected. A fixed schedule accepts enabled plus strict HH:MM start_at and stop_at. Timing accepts a 50..10000 ms sample interval; non-photo triggers also accept a 1..300 second transition delay. Photo rejects transition delay because its state machine bypasses the generic delay. Patched RIC requires GPIO direction/output checks, checked coil release and independent ISP mode readback before updating its policy/cache. Auto uses the current day/night target, using day if unknown. An unchanged policy with freshly verified GPIO and ISP state repairs its cache without GPIO or ISP writes. Changed policies or unconfirmed state use checked actuation and coil release. Control independently checks RIC and RVD, saves and reads the ircut.mode file value. Failure after application begins is partial_apply; explicitly reload and retry. When thresholds are submitted, Control also requires matching runtime values before save and exact independent disk values and a matching saved trigger after save. Timing requires matching live values, config-save and independent mapped disk readback; RIC gates exposure reads with a monotonic next-poll deadline despite early IPC wakeups, measures non-photo delay with monotonic elapsed time and clears evidence on gaps, cooldown, transitions and relevant setting changes. Only a status-ok exposure reply with the active trigger's bounded integer fields can advance detector, Photo or cooldown state. In Auto, the fixed schedule drives the checked RIC GPIO/ISP path; forced Day or Night has priority. Start is inclusive, stop exclusive, crossing midnight is supported and equal times mean Day all day. GET separates saved values, active ownership, target and application_ok. An active schedule may report target:null only with application_ok:false when local time or the first post-Auto poll is unavailable; settings POST still requires a known successfully applied target. Entering or leaving schedule ownership clears unfinished detector and Photo phase evidence. Solar scheduling accepts the exact sun object below and is mutually exclusive with the fixed schedule. GPIO configuration is not accepted. Automation accepts automation:{paused:boolean}; pause keeps RIC IPC and manual Day/Night available while stopping sensor, fixed and solar owners. Resume clears prior elapsed, count, cooldown, schedule, solar and Photo phase evidence, then clock owners recompute and sensors require fresh samples. Selecting Auto while paused does not resume automation. automatic_outputs:{color:boolean,ircut:boolean} controls only automatic participation; explicit Day/Night still owns both outputs and the existing IR850 policy. confirmation:{day,night} accepts integers 1..255 for luma, gain and ADC and requires both the direction count and existing elapsed delay. Defaults of one preserve prior behavior. Photo reports generic confirmation unsupported because its phase/ring algorithm has distinct counters, not because of a hardware limit. loglevel accepts fatal|error|warn|info|debug|trace for checked live RIC application and persistent readback. Every new mutation requires matching live state, config-save, exact independent disk values and final live state; config-file equality alone is not success.

raptor.daynight_initial_mode.semantics: Optional restart-only RIC startup policy. default means Day until automation takes over; it is not automatic detection. Forced mode wins and an active fixed or solar schedule may replace the startup target immediately. Saving does not actuate GPIO or ISP outputs.

raptor.daynight_ir850_at_night.semantics: RIC GPIO61 Night-mode policy; distinct from hardware capability, legacy controls.ir850 and Preview output ownership.

oneOf.semantics: source=raptor, persistent=true. state is the confirmed ISP/output state or null; it is not physical filter position. saved_mode is read independently from disk or null when unknown. matches_saved compares live policy with saved policy only when current output/ISP confirmation is available. Optional thresholds reports trigger, supported, available, values, saved_values and matches_saved separately. Optional timing reports capability, live values, saved values and matches_saved separately. Photo reports transition_delay_supported false, a null live transition delay and only its saved sample interval. Missing file keys use documented RIC defaults on GET; POST readback requires explicit saved keys. This is not boot or continuous automatic-detection evidence. Optional sun reports supported, available, the exact five-field values object, active, target day|night|null, condition normal|polar_day|polar_night|null, application_ok, independently read saved_values and matches_saved. Clock or calculation failure is active with null target/condition and application_ok:false. Forced modes retain configured solar values but set active:false. Optional startup separates configured, independently saved and boot_active default|day|night policies. matches_saved is false when disk readback is unavailable; restart_required is null until saved state is known, otherwise it compares saved with boot_active. Optional ir850_at_night is the live RIC Night-mode GPIO61 policy; saved_ir850_at_night is an independent disk observation and ir850_at_night_matches_saved compares them. It is not hardware-present metadata and is not the legacy controls.ir850 alias. Optional automation separates live paused, saved_paused and matches_saved. Optional automatic_outputs separates configured color/IR-cut participation and saved equality from color_owner, ircut_owner, current ISP color_state and last confirmed ircut_commanded_state; commanded state is not mechanical filter position. Optional confirmation returns direction counts and saved equality for luma, gain and ADC, while Photo returns supported:false, available:false and null values. Optional loglevel separates the live RIC level, saved_value and matches_saved. Paused fixed/solar objects are inactive and cannot actuate. A post-mutation readback mismatch is partial_apply and requires reload plus explicit retry. Optional service_enabled reports RIC service ownership separately from supported hardware and automation pause. False requires available:false, state:null and unavailable nested controls; automatic output owners are disabled with null live states. Earlier RIC omits this field and exits when disabled, so a valid older response is treated as service-enabled. Disabled service settings POST is refused before any mutation command. The read-only service field does not enable live service ownership.

ir850_policy.semantics: Optional for older native RIC. Missing disk key defaults true on GET; POST requires explicit exact disk readback. Preview ownership persists until a whole mode selection.

automation.semantics: Pause affects automatic owners only and never stops RIC IPC or manual Day/Night.

automatic_outputs.semantics: Participation policy, ownership and actual/command readback are distinct observations. Owners are automatic|manual when the service is enabled, or disabled when service_enabled:false; disabled owners require null color_state and ircut_commanded_state.

confirmation.semantics: Generic direction counts are unavailable for Photo's distinct algorithm.

service_enabled.semantics: Configured service ownership loaded at RIC startup; false is disabled, not unsupported hardware. Passive demand-driven OSD gain observations may continue without Day/Night actuation.

routes.secret_semantics: Nested secret names are null with matching _set flags. Omitted, null, or empty secret fields preserve stored values.

response_schema.semantics: Raptor-only checked ROD IPC. saved.available, saved.id, enabled and full typed entries are independent from published.id, generation, signed status, freshness and matches_saved. POST always retries an identical full replacement and succeeds only after native save/readback and fresh matching publication; any failure after dispatch is partial_apply. Gain remains an explicitly unavailable entry because no non-blocking all-mode producer exists. Hardware raster OSD availability is independent. If ROD IPC is absent the route is service_unavailable; the UI retains its draft and does not replace unknown saved entries with an empty table.

routes.secret_semantics: Named metadata has no credentials. User format strings are validated literal token templates and are never passed to printf.
The fixed hardware map contains no secrets. Pin numbers, ir940 and white are never accepted on POST.
JSON diagnostic sources mask secret fields before encoding.
The fixed report has no credential files and direct upload is forbidden.

semantics.backend_busy: 503 retryable pre-apply rejection: another Control media mutation holds the lock. No command from this rejected request was issued; explicitly retry after the active change completes.
semantics.raptor: source:raptor; persistent:true only with checked-config RVD support. POST accepts at least one supported setting and validates up to 15 scalar integer values: backlight 0..10, hflip/vflip 0..1, anti_flicker 0..2 and the other eleven fields 0..255. The checked batch maps backlight, wide_dynamic_range, tone, defog and noise_reduction to backlight_comp, drc_strength, highlight_depress, defog_strength and sinter. exposure_compensation maps to ae_comp; flip keys remain hflip and vflip. anti_flicker maps to the native sensor.antiflicker key: 0 is Off, 1 is 50 Hz and 2 is 60 Hz. Its field reports SDK observed_value, configured_value, independently read saved_value and matches_saved; malformed SDK values and read failures remain unavailable. It preflights every requested HAL setter/getter pair, applies the batch, requires exact SDK readback for thirteen fields, saves config and independently reads mapped image keys from disk. T31 noise_reduction is the source-proven exception: the SDK has a setter but no getter, so successful startup or a current setter call records an acknowledged configured value; transient getter failures never use this path. The optional white_balance object is an exact {mode,rgain,bgain} triplet: mode is 0..9, mode 1 is Manual, and gains are 0..1024. RVD applies and reads the triplet through the grouped T31 SDK operation, persists core_wb_mode/wb_rgain/wb_bgain, and restores them at startup. Automatic and preset live gains are null rather than being described as AWB statistics; configured gains remain explicit and cannot change outside Manual mode. Control requires live, independent disk and final-live equality before white_balance.matches_saved is true. A failed or malformed WB disk/config observation leaves the scalar imaging response usable, exposes null WB evidence and disables only WB mutation when its retained configured triplet is incomplete. The optional WB disk read has its own 150 ms deadline. Post-mutation failure is partial_apply; explicitly retry even unchanged values. Older RVD remains live-only with persistent:false.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted or returned.

response_schema.semantics: The compatibility file route retains existing media browsing and mutations through Raptor. GET ?cd= supports / and the fixed stream0, stream1 and timelapse roots beneath /mnt/mmcblk0p1/raptor, with optional &cursor= continuation. Only closed MP4/JPEG files with matching owner and metadata markers are offered and marked deletable. POST ?rm= accepts exactly one such file: the bounded SD worker reopens the file and marker through held directory descriptors, verifies exact device/inode/size/mtime and single-link identity, unlinks only those two names, syncs the directory and invalidates list continuations; active, pending, invalidated, internal, unrelated, hardlinked or symlinked files are excluded. On a device-verified vfat mount only, completion markers use two-second mtime slots with zero nanoseconds; an old odd-second marker may match the same even-second slot after remount. Owner, size, path and live descriptor identity checks remain exact. ext4 and exfat timestamps are compared exactly. Unknown mounts never enable FAT matching. A previous closed RMR clip remains readable while a new segment is active. Each page returns at most 512 entries and scans at most 4096 entries from a held directory iterator. An early scan boundary may return an empty page with next_cursor. Follow next_cursor until null. At most four iterators are retained; cursors expire after two idle minutes, rotate on use, bind the path and directory device/inode/mtime/ctime, and are invalidated on observed directory change, eviction or process restart. Invalid/stale cursors return invalid_request; refresh from the first page. Entries are sorted within each page, not globally. Unchanged directories are traversed without duplicates; changing directories are not snapshots and coarse filesystem timestamps or in-place marker/file changes can escape directory-change detection. Reads never create directories. All SD open/stat/read_dir/marker-read/statvfs work runs in one dedicated reader with one queued job. Request wait is bounded by the earlier of its deadline and 150 ms; full queue returns backend_busy. Scan iterations reserve 40 ms for completion, but a blocked syscall may outlive the caller. Expired queued jobs are skipped before disk work. No replacement thread, per-timeout thread or identity cache is created.

routes.secret_semantics: Only media roots are accepted. Configuration and credential paths are outside the route allowlist.

semantics.probe: DNS and TCP reachability failures are successful diagnostic responses with success=false and bounded sanitized output; malformed requests remain errors.

routes.secret_semantics: Scan and probe responses never contain the stored Wi-Fi password.

semantics.raptor.audio: Raptor maps microphone and speaker enable, built microphone codecs, ALC and four audio levels, plus NS, HPF and AGC when effects were built. Input/output enable and processing use checked owner readback; levels and ALC use HAL readback. NS is 0=off and 1..4=SDK levels 0..3. Disabled input or output settings require an explicit enable and reload before editing their dependent controls. Speaker levels are independent of microphone mute; microphone levels and ALC require mute to be known false. The DCS-6100LHV2 A1 profile reports mic_is_digital=false and force_stereo=false as fixed non-writable topology. Prudynt buffer warning/capacity and microphone tap fields are null with explicit unsupported ownership because RAD has no equivalent controls. Successful POST requires live readback, config-save and independent disk readback including dependent processing, codec sample-rate and requested enable keys. Failure after apply begins is partial_apply.
semantics.stream*.buffers: 1 through 65535 when enabled; minus one only when disabled
semantics.stream*.fps: 1 through 30 when enabled; zero only when disabled
semantics.raptor.motion: Accepts motion.enabled boolean and optional sensitivity integer 0..4 when enabled is true and the currently running standard move algorithm exposes checked sensitivity. The native SDK getter must confirm every ROI sensitivity and preserve dimensions, ROI geometry and skip count. Control requires owner and sensitivity readback, config-save and independent disk values. Stopped detection requires enable then reload before editing sensitivity. Additive ROI editing accepts all four existing roi_0_x/y and roi_1_x/y integer edges plus roi_count=1 with enabled=true. Coordinates use detection-frame pixels and exclusive end edges. A checked single-region-v1 standard Move getter must expose matching frame dimensions; policy limits coordinates to 16384, a minimum 2x2 rectangle and observed counts 1..51. ROI changes pause worker and receive, update the retained SDK channel, preserve sensitivity and skip count, and require independent SDK readback before explicit resume. Unconfirmed SDK writes block resume until an explicit ROI retry. Control checks live geometry, enabled state, save, independent inclusive disk tuple and final live geometry. Multi-region layouts are observed but can only be replaced with one explicit rectangle; no inferred default ROI is written. Errors after apply begins are partial_apply; unchanged values remain explicit for persistence retry. Event actions accept video_length 1..86400, send2storage, playonspeaker and speaker_repeats 1..3 only as a complete set. Control requires native cache preflight/readback, one config-save, independent disk equality and final live equality. The in-process action worker consumes processed Active transitions, starts only a stopped RMR owner, extends its own deadline and uses a user-generation guard before stopping. The speaker action uses only RAD built-in clip motion; output must already be enabled at 16 kHz and Privacy must be off. Talkback preempts the clip. No arbitrary path, shell command or child process is accepted.
semantics.raptor.osd: Accepts one to five supported OSD text fields: format, fill_color, outline_color, font_size and enabled. Each requires its current capability flag. Colors use #RRGGBBAA with independent 0..255 alpha. font_size is 16..48 main-stream pixels, not legacy scale; the default profile uses 48 and substream text has a 12-pixel floor. enabled controls named text only, not ROD, receipt layers or Privacy. ROD validates glyph bounds and reuses hardware regions; Control requires matching ROD/RVD operation receipts, config-save and independent disk readback. Partial failure requires explicit retry. The named text canvas supports a BGRA background. Structured metadata remains unavailable.
semantics.raptor.privacy: Only a privacy domain containing one enabled boolean is accepted. Checked-startup RVD and every configured or socket-present RAD/RHD participant must advertise support before mutation. Control requires complete application, independent matching video/audio/JPEG owner readback, config-save, independent privacy.enabled disk readback and final unchanged participant/readback agreement. Any failure after mutation begins is partial_apply; no automatic rollback or retry. Explicit unchanged values are accepted for saving retries. RVD owns the shared privacy.enabled key; RVD/RAD/RHD load it before video publisher, microphone ring or HTTP listener startup.

raptor_stream_gop.semantics: Only GOP in one or both stream domains is accepted. Bounds are application policy, not a verified SDK range. Require an active non-JPEG H264/H265 owner with an exactly readable DEFAULT, PYRAMIDAL or SMARTP GOP mode, checked startup and get/set HAL functions. Preflight all requested streams before mutation. After each setter require independent exact SDK length and mode readback; then config-save, independent disk gop read and final live read for all requested streams. Any failure after mutation begins is partial_apply. An unchanged requested value still repairs cache and retries persistence. No max_gop, bitrate, GOP mode or other stream writes through this GOP operation. FPS and restart-only GOP mode use separate requests.

raptor_stream_fps.semantics: Exactly one stream containing only fps per POST. Semantic sensor-0 main/sub IDs map directly to checked get-stream-fps/set-stream-fps; never legacy set-fps, config-save or another setter. Daemon owns lifecycle, SDK verification, atomic metadata and persistence. No automatic retry/restart. Missing/incompatible replies disable FPS editing. Other settings remain governed by existing capabilities.

raptor_stream_encoding.semantics: One or both stream domains may be supplied; each contains exactly mode and bitrate. Control validates and preflights all streams before mutation, applies the paired native setter, requires exact independent SDK readback, saves once, reads each disk section independently and obtains final live readback. Any failure after mutation begins is partial_apply. No automatic retry or rollback. Bounds and step are application policy; exact SDK acceptance and readback are still required. FIXQP uses the separate restart-only rate-control contract; SMART remains unavailable because this live contract requires a checked target bitrate.

raptor_stream_fixqp.semantics: One or both stream domains may be supplied; each contains exactly mode and qp_init. The operation is available only when the active or requested mode is FIXQP. It updates startup configuration without calling a live SDK setter, preserves the saved bitrate, saves once, reads mode, QP and bitrate independently from disk, and confirms active HAL mode and FIXQP initial QP remain unchanged. pending_restart truthfully compares active and saved state. A full camera-stack restart is required. Any failure after mutation begins is partial_apply; explicit unchanged values retry persistence.

raptor_stream_profile.semantics: One or both stream domains may be supplied; each contains exactly profile. Profiles 0, 1 and 2 map to H.264 Baseline, Main and High. Control preflights all requested active H264 owners before mutation. RVD performs a full restart and requires exact encoder plus recreated ring profile_idc readback. Control saves once, reads each disk section independently and obtains final live readback. Any failure after restart begins is partial_apply and latches codec recovery until full RVD bootstrap. H265 profile control is unsupported.

raptor_osd.semantics: One OSD domain per request, no unknown fields. Capability-gated text fields only. Format must be printable ASCII without surrounding whitespace, hash or semicolon and use the supported strftime directives. Existing glyph canvas bounds are checked before publication. Text size, visibility and all three RGBA colors are saved and restored by the native startup loader; device effects and reboot acceptance require matching-firmware testing.

raptor_stream_gop_mode.semantics: One or both stream domains may be supplied; each contains only gop_mode. DEFAULT, PYRAMIDAL and SMARTP are the exact pinned T31 SDK GOP-control modes supported for H264/H265. SMARTP is not the unsupported SMART rate-control alias. The operation updates startup configuration without a live SDK setter, saves once, reads each disk section independently and confirms the active HAL mode remains unchanged. Startup rejects an unknown or silently substituted SDK mode. pending_restart truthfully compares active and saved mode, and a full camera-stack restart is required. Existing GOP length remains independently live and checked in every admitted mode. Attribute readback does not prove emitted bitstream structure; device bitstream verification remains required. Mode-specific same-scene and long-term-reference parameters are not exposed without a sourced admission contract.

raptor_stream_enable.semantics: Only stream1 containing exactly enabled is accepted. The current software pipeline requires stream0; main-stream disable remains unimplemented and this is not a hardware-limit claim. Stream1 changes update startup configuration only and never call a live setter or restart automatically. Control preflights Motion FrameSource-1 ownership, recorder1 autostart, and active, transitioning or unknown recorder1 state before disable; saves once; reads the disk value independently; and confirms active state remains unchanged. When configured and saved state disagree, an otherwise untouched form retries the configured value; explicitly selecting the saved value rolls configuration back. Other stream saves include this reconciliation before any later config-save. A saved pending-disable blocks Motion enable, recorder1 autostart enable, and manual or event recorder starts. Re-enable does not require an existing recorder1 socket. Applying either direction requires a full camera-stack restart and subsequent active readback.

oneOf.semantics: source=raptor; five level values are numbers or null with complete supported/available/value/min/max metadata. Input, output, codec and processing values remain null when unknown or unavailable. codecs_built and effects_built distinguish unbuilt capabilities from current availability. input_readback and processing_readback are owner, not SDK getter evidence.

source=raptor; persistent=true identifies checked configuration support. enabled is observed monitoring or null if ownership is inconsistent. saved_enabled is an independent disk read. Sensitivity is a uniform SDK value 0..4 or null; availability is limited to a running standard move algorithm. saved_sensitivity is an independent disk value or null when unknown/invalid. Each matches_saved flag compares its live value with disk; neither proves startup or actual motion detection. Additive roi is null for older daemons, otherwise contains supported, available, applied, frame_width, frame_height, count, single, saved_single and matches_saved. Available geometry can come from an allocated active or paused standard Move channel; unavailable geometry stays null. single and saved_single use the four existing exclusive-edge API keys; single is null for multi-region state and saved_single is null for non-single or unreadable saved layouts. applied=false permits explicit repair with known geometry and never implies success. ROI matches_saved requires known applied single geometry equal to independently read saved geometry. GET additionally reports the live and saved event action set, its agreement, current RMR availability and compatible RAD control reachability, last speaker playback state, worker running state, event-owned channel and bounded storage, speaker, rate-limit and queue-drop counters. speaker_action_available does not prove playback readiness or the presence of the alert file; playback requires enabled 16 kHz output, mute and Privacy off, no active talkback and the installed clip. Home Assistant retains MQTT publishing. RAD accepts only the fixed built-in motion alert, one to three repeats; output disable, Privacy, action disable and talkback cancel or preempt it without destroying a foreign ring. Other destinations are unimplemented service integrations; they are not classified as hardware-unsupported. Persistent privacy has a separate privacy-domain form.

source=raptor; persistent=true identifies checked save support. available and per-field flags describe current text targets. matches_saved compares supported live text settings with independent disk values and is false when unavailable. This is a saved/live comparison, not boot-failure evidence. SDK submission receipt is not physical pixel readback. font_size is a numeric 16..48 value when its capability is present, otherwise null. fields.enabled advertises text visibility control; hidden text can remain available for re-enabling. Size and RGBA changes reuse allocated hardware bitmap regions rather than restarting video. fields.fill_alpha and fields.outline_alpha gate translucent text colors for compatibility with older ROD versions; background_color has its own capability. Fill, outline and background alpha are composed into BGRA pixels; physical blending remains a device acceptance check.

source=raptor and persistent=true identify checked-startup support. enabled is the matching video and required RAD/RHD owner state, or null if partial/unavailable. saved_enabled is an independent canonical true/false disk value, defaults false only when the key is absent, and is null when unreadable/invalid. matches_saved is true only for matching known live and saved values. Mask and mute reports are owner/checked SDK setter evidence, not independent physical pixels or microphone readback. Host startup guards do not establish device acceptance.

source=raptor,persistent=true. stream_id equals requested domain. supported is the checked-startup default-GOP capability; available also requires active video ownership and successful bounded SDK getter. gop is an integer 1..65535 when available, otherwise null. saved_gop is an independently read explicit disk value or null; absent gop is not an invented saved default. matches_saved compares known live and disk values, not physical output. POST returns status=accepted,persistent=true only after all checks. encoding_control is independently supported and contains either supported:false,available:false or complete checked live/saved rate-control mode and target bitrate metadata. Its matches_saved is true only for known exact live and independent disk agreement. profile_control is independently supported only for active H264 and contains either supported:false,available:false or complete live/saved profile metadata for 0=Baseline, 1=Main and 2=High. enable_control is independent and contains either supported:null,available:false,editable:false or a complete owner report with supported, available, editable, required, active_enabled, configured_enabled, saved_available, saved_enabled, configured_matches_saved, pending_restart, Motion and recorder disable blockers, recorder-state certainty and apply=full-camera-restart. saved_enabled and pending_restart are null when independent disk state is unavailable. stream0 is required and non-editable by the current software pipeline; stream1 is restart-only editable when its observations are complete.

semantics.backend_busy: 503 retryable pre-apply rejection: another Control media mutation holds the lock. No command from this rejected request was issued; explicitly retry after the active change completes.
semantics.raptor_fps: GET adds fps_control. A missing, malformed or unreachable FPS backend is supported:false,available:false without disabling existing GOP. A validated receipt contains supported:true,available,status,stream_id,recovery_required,persistence_pending,live_applied,persisted,fps,monitoring with related/active/paused/receiving/thread_owned booleans. live_applied/persisted are boolean or null; fps is integer 1..30 or null. Availability requires a verified configuration, no recovery, and status ok or persistence pending. POST HTTP 200 is an operation receipt, not an acceptance claim: status accepted,persistent true only with checked status ok and exact FPS, live_applied true,persisted true. Otherwise status error,persistent false with fps_result retaining exact known/unknown outcomes. Incompatible or lost mutation replies are partial_apply errors with unknown outcome. Arbitrary daemon error strings are not forwarded. Persistence-only explicit retry is the same single-stream value. Failed motion resume preserves live_applied true,persisted true but status error. These are SDK configuration reports, not physical cadence evidence.
semantics.raptor_encoding: GET adds encoding_control independently of GOP and FPS. A complete object reports supported, available, rc_mode, bitrate, saved_rc_mode, saved_bitrate, matches_saved, bitrate_min=1000, bitrate_max=100000000, bitrate_step=1000 and modes=[CBR,VBR,CAPPED_VBR,CAPPED_QUALITY]. Unknown or malformed native state disables editing. POST accepts paired mode and bitrate for one or both streams and claims accepted,persistent=true only after preflight, exact live apply readback, config-save, disk readback and final live readback. This is SDK configuration evidence, not emitted bitrate measurement.
semantics.raptor_fixqp: GET adds rc_config_control independently of live target-bitrate control. A complete object reports supported, available, active_mode, active_qp, saved_available, saved_mode, saved_qp, matches_saved, pending_restart, qp_min=0, qp_max=51, qp_default=35 and modes including FIXQP. active_qp is present only for active FIXQP; saved_qp retains the selected startup QP. POST accepts mode plus qp_init and does not claim a live transition. The numeric range follows the matched HAL H.264 and H.265 QP representation; the matched SDK header does not separately document iInitialQP limits, so exact HAL startup readback remains required.
semantics.raptor_profile: GET adds profile_control independently of GOP, FPS and rate control. A complete object reports supported, available, recovery_required, profile, saved_profile, matches_saved and profiles=[0,1,2]. POST accepts profile for one or both H264 streams and claims accepted,persistent=true only after all-owner preflight, full restart, exact encoder and ring profile_idc readback, config-save, disk readback and final live readback. H265 is unsupported. This is SDK configuration and owner evidence, not emitted bitstream measurement.
semantics.raptor_buffers: GET adds read-only buffer_control. supported:null means native transport or schema failure; supported:false means a validated reply reports no getter. A supported reply separates active_buffers from exact T31 SDK nrVBs, configured_buffers from loaded config, and saved_buffers from independent disk readback. Unknown values are null. available and saved_available identify observed values; match flags require known equality. editable is false. The dcs6100lhv2-a1-42m-22m-v1 profile requires one buffer per stream but hardware_limit_known remains false. profile_admitted requires all three values to equal one; a false flag alone does not prove an invalid profile when readback is incomplete.
semantics.raptor_stream_enable: GET adds enable_control independently of other stream controls. active_enabled is current RVD owner state, configured_enabled is the loaded startup value, and saved_enabled is an independent nullable disk read. saved_available identifies a known disk value, configured_matches_saved compares loaded and saved startup state, and pending_restart is true or false only when saved state is known; otherwise it is null. POST accepts stream1 enabled only, reports accepted,persistent=true after checked save, disk readback and unchanged active readback, and requires a later full camera-stack restart. Disable blockers cover Motion FrameSource 1, recorder1 autostart and active, transitioning or unknown recorder1 state. Pending disable also rejects later Motion enable, recorder autostart enable and manual or Motion-event recorder starts. Main disable remains an open software-ownership implementation, not a hardware limitation. The WebUI materializes configured state during a disk mismatch, retries it on an untouched save, permits explicit rollback to the saved state, and reconciles enable before another stream operation can save stale cache. Application acceptance requires matching active/configured readback. Timezone and SD-format participant sets retain active recorder1 through pending disable and omit it only after checked inactive startup; unknown membership fails closed.

routes.secret_semantics: Nested Prudynt secrets are null with matching _set flags and are write-only on POST.

request_schema.semantics: Prudynt retains one partial video or timelapse domain. Raptor accepts video with required channel 0 or 1 matching the optional query. GET defaults to channel 0. Fixed mount, stream root and filename cannot change. Mutable settings: autostart, cleanup_enabled, duration 1..86400 seconds, limit 1..1000 closed clips, min_free_mb 1..1000000 MiB, check_interval 1..86400 seconds. Raptor ?domain=timelapse accepts exactly one partial timelapse object: enabled, interval 1..1440 minutes, keep_days 0..365, preset_enabled, presets with ircut/ir850/color booleans. Mount /mnt/mmcblk0p1, filepath raptor/timelapse and filename unix-seconds-sequence.jpg are fixed. The query cannot be combined with channel.

response_schema.semantics: Raptor envelope has source raptor, persistent true, actual video settings, saved_video or null, matches_saved, runtime or null, storage_available, free_mb or null, boot_pending, cleanup_ok, fixed mounts, current Timelapse policy and timelapse_supported true. POST returns accepted/persistent only after apply, live readback, config-save, independent disk readback and final live readback. No request stops, restarts or saves another recorder. Autostart applies at boot. Retention deletes only own marked closed files, with fixed-memory scans in one detached worker per RMR and at most 32 deletions per batch; active, unmarked and other-stream files remain. Both owners share the physical SD free-space threshold; insufficient space reports no_space. The main control/frame loop uses cached SD observations; a missing or older-than-2.5-second sample reports storage_unknown. New segment creation still verifies mount identity. Background scans retain only the oldest 32 candidates and full deletion batches continue after 100 ms, so large directories converge without a total-entry ceiling. Host verification does not establish device acceptance. Timelapse query returns source raptor, domain timelapse, persistent true, available, timelapse, saved_timelapse or null, matches_saved, fixed mounts and runtime phase/last_error/preset_restore/successes/last_success/next_due/cleanup_blocked. POST accepted/persistent follows atomic config write, fsync, independent parse/readback and live worker policy update. One worker restores /etc/raptor-timelapse.json at startup and captures main JPEG immediately when enabled, then interval minutes after each attempt without catch-up bursts. HTTP and SD work never hold the Preview mutation lock or run in recorder control/frame loops. Forced day/night is required for presets; checked per-field restoration stops on Privacy or user-setting generation changes and pauses captures until explicit settings save after control reconciliation. Privacy unknown/on or generation changes before/after capture, staging and publication invalidate only the new image. New files are exclusive, completed files have matching own metadata markers, staging is excluded from completed listing/retention. The pending marker remains through the final Privacy/settings fence; its removal exposes an already accepted image. Later Privacy changes do not invalidate completed images. Persisted pending state also blocks listing after a backend restart. Rollback requires ownership/identity and failed removal remains cleanup_failed with captures paused. Keep_days zero preserves all; enabled retention removes at most 32 own expired closed files per pass and converges without a total-entry ceiling. There is no atomic guarantee between a filesystem syscall and Privacy, nor cancellation of a hung disk syscall. Old completed images, main/sub recordings and other SD files are preserved. Timelapse UI polls status every two seconds while open without replacing draft form values; disposal stops polling. Pinned RHD snapshot parks its cursor at write_seq+1, so it requires a ring publication after HTTP request acceptance rather than returning an already cached JPEG. Neither this sequence nor control readback proves exposure after preset application or physical IR/ISP settling; preset image correctness remains unqualified until device verification.

routes.secret_semantics: No secret fields are accepted or returned.

semantics.heartbeat.raptor_recording: rec_ch0 and rec_ch1 reflect separate managed RMR writer observations, with null for missing or unconfirmed state. Optional rec_chN_file_closed and rec_chN_available booleans and rec_chN_reason values no_sd, no_space, storage_unknown, video_unavailable, writer_error, starting, stopping or null explain start availability. No SD reports known Off plus available false; Live disables start while allowing stop of an active writer. A null recording observation with file_closed false retains an explicit Stop recording recovery action until independent closure. Each owner read has a 150 ms sub-deadline. Legacy fields remain available for API compatibility; Raptor fills only verified values.
semantics.heartbeat.raptor_timelapse: timelapse_enabled observes the native service policy from memory without I/O or waiting for a state lock. Initialized, started services with a confirmed policy report true or false; unstarted, stopped, uninitialized, failed policy load/save or unavailable state observations report null. A missing saved policy is a confirmed disabled default. Enabled describes policy, not a successful capture; capture errors do not imply disabled.
semantics.heartbeat.motion_enabled: Raptor Motion producer is currently monitoring
semantics.media.streams.*.enabled: configured enabled and fps greater than zero and buffers not minus one
semantics.media/metrics: bounded Prometheus text read directly from the media backend Unix socket without a child process
semantics.motion.queue: bounded ingress counters with capacity, current depth, high-water, dropped and safely coalesced observations
semantics.raptor: RVD provides sparse per-stream configured and observed states, semantic stream_id/jpeg identity and bounded metadata. Video available requires configured and available RVD video metadata, independently of JPEG state. snapshot_url additionally requires the corresponding validated RVD JPEG slot and RHD jpeg_available slot; aggregate counts never imply availability. RVD JPEG available describes active production, not idle snapshot capability. An idle slot permits a bounded snapshot request only with explicit stream_id/jpeg identity, available:false and both FPS recovery/persistence flags false. Configured live video is still required. The RHD HTTP request creates per-slot ring demand and waits past the existing frame sequence; only a successful bounded response establishes capture. HA and Timelapse keep their privacy checks before capture and before publication. RHD and RSD status reads each have a 150 ms sub-deadline. RSD failure omits RTSP metadata without removing JPEG streams. RIC mode and optional RVD IVS observations populate heartbeat; unavailable measurements stay null.
semantics.media.streams.*: Additive optional width, height, fps, format, bitrate, gop and rtsp_endpoint metadata. Preview does not fetch backend-specific configuration. Endpoints are validated paths, never upstream URLs. No passwords or usernames are added to runtime responses.
semantics.media.rtsp: Optional port from validated backend metadata. Absent when RSD is unavailable.
semantics.daynight.raptor: History is a process-local ring of at most 300 successful heartbeat observations and 63 KiB of encoded sample data. Checked RVD get-exposure supplies nonnegative finite total_gain, exposure_us, AE luma, EV and white-balance gains; brightness_pct is derived only from AE luma divided by 255. Sensors reports the active checked RIC threshold shape and current checked exposure independently. Raptor has no percentage night/day threshold pair, so those fields are null; unavailable exposure is current:null and never disables supported RIC policy controls.
semantics.heartbeat.controls_supported: Optional typed daynight, motion and privacy capability booleans; capability is independent of enabled state. Missing map preserves the documented compatibility shape.
semantics.heartbeat.raptor_ir: ircut_state and ir850_state are 0 or 1 only from strict RIC output observations; unsupported, unavailable, missing or malformed states remain null. Standalone output changes do not select whole day/night policy or change ISP/color.
semantics.heartbeat.raptor_audio: mic_enabled and spk_enabled come from bounded RAD owner observations. Disabled but known owners report false; missing, malformed or unknown observations remain null. Audio level values alone never imply enabled state.
semantics.heartbeat.nullability: Control booleans may be null when the selected backend has no verified observation. Null is not false. Legacy response fields remain available for compatibility; Raptor does not infer values for them.
semantics.imaging.raptor: source:raptor; brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpness, backlight, wide_dynamic_range, tone, defog, noise_reduction, hue, dpc_strength, exposure_compensation, hflip, vflip and anti_flicker. Each field separates supported from available and declares its exact range; unavailable values are null. Optional verification distinguishes sdk-readback from T31 noise-reduction sdk-setter-config; observed_value is null for the latter and configured_value is exposed only as available after matching runtime setter acknowledgement. Anti-flicker uses 0 Off, 1 50 Hz and 2 60 Hz with SDK readback; its observed, configured and saved values remain separate, and matches_saved requires all three to agree. Checked-config RVD adds persistent:true with SDK, save and independent mapped disk verification. Older RVD remains live-only.
semantics.privacy.raptor: Acceptance requires successful video masks and every configured or socket-present RAD/RHD participant, then independent state readback. Partial application reports failure and retains acquired masks without automatic rollback.
semantics.system.media: May be null when only shared host state is available. Legacy fields remain unchanged for compatibility.
semantics.motion.raptor: version 1, source raptor, supported, available, monitoring, active, receiving. available is false when active and receive ownership disagree. active forwards RVD's detection bit only when supported, monitoring and receiving are true. available requires support and matching monitoring/receive ownership. When unavailable, active=false is a placeholder, not confirmed inactivity; heartbeat motion_enabled and motion_active are null. A stopped detector reports active=false even if RVD retains its old detection bit. Each read queries RVD anew, with a 150 ms motion sub-deadline for heartbeat; disconnect or malformed replies cannot reuse a prior observation. Native Motion queue and sink counters are absent because RVD does not produce them.
semantics.raptor.fps_recovery: Paired optional fps_recovery_required/fps_persistence_pending flags must both be booleans. Either true requires available:false and null daemon FPS. Public runtime omits that unconfirmed FPS while retaining bounded dimensions and the other stream; no cached rate is substituted.

routes.secret_semantics: Runtime responses contain no credentials, tokens, artifact contents, or unbounded event payloads.
The compatibility response is identical to the canonical runtime sensor response and contains no credentials or device identifiers.

semantics.raptor: Reports the selected Raptor HA worker using the existing response shape. Connected means MQTT connection, not camera or JPEG acceptance. Entity availability requires both global connection availability and a fresh checked owner observation. Missing/null owner state clears retained state and marks the entity offline, never OFF. RVD motion polling is nominally 500 ms with a 150 ms read deadline; periodic full state refresh is capped at 5 s, excluding bounded reads and other worker work. Reconnect forces fresh state and invalidates prior image availability. JPEG capture requires checked RVD producer and RHD slot with Privacy false before and after capture; missing JPEG remains unavailable even when video works. HA JPEG is main-stream only, at most 256 KiB, non-retained QoS 0 with at most one pending image and a 250 ms local write drain. HTTP capture does not hold the media mutation lock. Control Privacy transitions invalidate captures, including changes later reversed or failed. Only the final Privacy check (150 ms) and image write (250 ms) share the mutation lock; Preview can still receive Busy in that bounded phase. Worker generation changes discard captured data. Broker transport and physical device acceptance remain separate gates.
semantics.webui_polling: The Services HA status poll is single-flight. Actions await any older poll, then request fresh state. Only one five-second follow-up timer is scheduled, and navigation disposes it without replacing form drafts.

routes.secret_semantics: The response contains bounded counters and sanitized error classes, never broker credentials or raw library errors.
Destination passwords, tokens, client secrets, and API keys are write-only and redacted on GET.

semantics.sd.device: One coherent removable-MMC identity derived from sysfs or an allowlisted live mount; no card serial is returned.
semantics.sd.filesystems: Bounded mounted-MMC usage records from the same mount-table snapshot.
semantics.sd.format: One queued FAT32 operation for the exact D-Link mmcblk0p1 mount. Control binds the request to the private live card generation and a persistent versioned Unix-socket worker revalidates it before ordinary unmount, partition-only mkfs, remount and writable verification.
semantics.raptor.sd: GET reports the fixed verified mmcblk0p1 mount; unmounted fixed-device presence never implies a mount, and unavailable capacity or usage is null. No card serial is returned. Formatting requires the exact writable mount, private CID and storage-worker socket. options contains the shared fat32 id/label/description object when supported. POST requires action=format, filesystem=fat32 and confirm=erase, queues one operation and exposes queued/running/succeeded/failed through GET. Maintenance bars new file reads/deletes, drains queued reads and directory descriptors, pauses and drains native timelapse, stops active RMR writers and independently verifies both file_closed states and both volatile RMR probe/retention pause acknowledgements. The existing worker rechecks card and device identity before ordinary unmount, partition-only mkfs and verified remount. A valid terminal result resumes maintenance and restores prior recording intent; an unconfirmed worker completion keeps recording, maintenance and file access paused, disables formatting, and requires an explicit normal reboot before recovery. Control neither cancels existing uhttpd transfers nor forces unmount; busy unmount prevents mkfs. Ordinary SD reads use one reader and one queued job with at most 150 ms caller wait. A stalled syscall creates no replacement worker. Active format GET uses the preformat snapshot plus current operation state, not fresh disk usage.

routes.secret_semantics: Storage responses contain no credentials or removable-media serial numbers. The card generation is used only on the local worker socket and is never returned.

GET reports only exists, POST atomically persists a mode-0600 rotation and returns the new value once, and DELETE removes it with parent-directory synchronization. The stored key is never returned later, an API key cannot manage this route, and mutations require a browser login at most 10 minutes old. These semantics belong to the Raptor WebUI service.

response_schema.semantics: Raptor file reads require an exact fixed recording path and optional play=1 or download=1. Every GET/range request uses the existing authenticated Control preflight. Its internal X-Thingino-File-Identity header binds device, inode, size and modification time to the descriptor opened by uhttpd through a no-symlink component walk. The header is consumed internally and never forwarded to the browser. Files must remain regular and single-linked. A missing identity cannot serve a Raptor recording. Large bodies and existing range handling stay in uhttpd; Control never buffers the recording. This is a metadata identity check, not a content digest or cancellation of already authorized reads. Raptor identity lookup uses the same dedicated bounded SD reader, takes the request deadline and returns backend_busy/backend_timeout explicitly. Non-file live preflight never enters the SD queue. Every file identity is a fresh request result; caller timeout does not prove completion or cancel a blocked disk syscall. Uhttpd body-read isolation remains outside this checkpoint.

routes.secret_semantics: Authorization is checked before stream headers. No credential is forwarded to a media backend or returned.
